                    ### Question
                    18-year-old girl who came to the Hospital for edema in lower limbs of 1 week of evolution, highlighting in the laboratory a proteinuria in the nephrotic range with hypoproteinemia and hypoalbuminemia. In the anamnesis he refers to recurrent oral aphthae, arthritis of small joints of the hands, malar rash and photosensitivity. In the etiological study, the presence of ANA and antiDNA with hypocomplementemia stands out. The determination of ANCA is negative. A renal biopsy is performed in which we could find any of these types of glomerulonephritis, EXCEPT:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Mesangial GNF.
opb. Necrotizing GNF paucinmune.
opc. Focal proliferative GNF.
opd. Diffuse proliferative GNF.
ope. Membranous GNF.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation and laboratory findings are highly suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), characterized by symptoms such as recurrent oral aphthae, arthritis, malar rash, photosensitivity, and laboratory findings of positive ANA and anti-DNA antibodies with hypocomplementemia. In SLE, lupus nephritis is a common renal manifestation, and the types of glomerulonephritis typically associated with lupus nephritis include mesangial, focal proliferative, diffuse proliferative, and membranous glomerulonephritis. Necrotizing glomerulonephritis, particularly the paucimmune type, is not typically associated with SLE, as it is more commonly linked to ANCA-associated vasculitis, which is not supported by the negative ANCA test in this case. Therefore, the renal biopsy would not be expected to show necrotizing glomerulonephritis paucimmune in this patient with SLE. The retrieved evidence paths support the association of SLE with antinuclear antibodies and hypocomplementemia, reinforcing the diagnosis of lupus nephritis and excluding necrotizing glomerulonephritis paucimmune as a likely finding.
